description:
ABOUT DEXMATE

Dexmate is building the foundation for physical AI — combining a new generation of robots with a universal Physical AI OS, making robots as easy to build and deploy as software. Today, robotics is fragmented, slow, and closed: most builders are forced to reinvent the same stack again and again, and most ideas never make it past the prototype stage. We exist to change that. Our mission is to democratize robotics by lowering the barrier to entry, delivering a plug-and-play platform for developers, researchers, and enterprises, and cultivating an open ecosystem that accelerates the evolution of physical AI.

If you want to help shape the next layer of human capability — and believe the future of robotics should be built together, not in isolation — we'd love to build it with you.


THE ROLE

Help Dexmate build reliable robots and release hardware, software, and firmware with confidence. As a Robot Validation & HIL Test Engineer, you will own automated test systems from hardware-in-the-loop (HIL) benches to whole-robot validation. You will build the rigs, tools, and test coverage that reveal integration failures, verify real-world performance, and give engineers clear evidence for design and release decisions.

This is a hands-on role spanning mechanical, electrical, and software engineering. You will help establish and operate our test lab, develop repeatable tests that run around the clock, and validate robots under conditions that reflect customer use. Working with hardware, firmware, controls, robot software, and release infrastructure teams, you will turn test results and field failures into more reliable products.


RESPONSIBILITIES

 - Design, build, and maintain modular HIL benches and automated test stations combining robot compute, controllers, sensors, actuators, mechanical fixtures, and simulated signals or loads. Build interface boards and harnesses, and work with equipment suppliers on custom stations.

 - Develop Python-based frameworks and command-line tools to configure test equipment, deploy software and firmware, execute tests, and collect synchronized measurements, logs, and bus traces.

 - Develop and execute subsystem and whole-robot functional tests covering mobility, manipulation, payload, terrain, continuous operation, and representative customer scenarios and environmental conditions. Assemble, configure, and prepare robots for testing.

 - Partner with mechanical, electrical, firmware, and software engineers to define coverage and acceptance criteria, execute validation plans, and automate long-duration durability and duty-cycle tests. Enable unattended overnight and weekend runs with alerts, interlocks, and automatic shutdowns, scaling to dozens of modules in parallel.

 - Validate test-station accuracy, repeatability, and stability; maintain equipment calibration, bench health checks, and safe operating procedures so engineers can trust the results.

 - Verify software, firmware, API, and protocol compatibility across robot hardware revisions. Check component versions and dependencies against defined release configurations to catch integration problems before deployment.

 - Build fault-injection and recovery tests for sensor faults, communication loss and latency, controller resets, interrupted power, and invalid configurations. Verify error reporting, safe-state behavior, and recovery using simulation or emulation where appropriate.

 - Validate installation, over-the-air (OTA) updates, interrupted upgrades, and rollback to known-good software and firmware configurations.

 - Integrate automated tests with the release team's CI/CD workflows, supporting targeted checks for code changes and broader nightly regression runs. Implement shared-station allocation, queueing, and automated reset and recovery.

 - Build data acquisition, logging, dashboards, and pass/fail reporting across test stations. Link results to code commits, hardware configurations, software and firmware versions, and test definitions; distinguish product failures from test-equipment issues.

 - Reproduce failures from lab testing and customer use, investigate root causes with the responsible engineers, verify fixes, and add regression coverage. Improve test reliability and close coverage gaps as the platform evolves.

 - Document test-system designs, procedures, and troubleshooting guides. Coordinate with technicians and manufacturing test teams to support consistent execution and reuse relevant tests while maintaining stable production test configurations.


MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS

 - Bachelor's degree in Mechatronics, Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Computer Science, Robotics, or a related field, or equivalent hands-on experience.

 - 4+ years of experience in robot validation, HIL testing, embedded systems validation, or test automation, including hands-on ownership of a hardware-based test system.

 - Strong Python programming skills and experience building maintainable test frameworks, automation tools, and data collection systems.

 - Proficiency in Linux, Git, and command-line workflows, with experience integrating automated tests into CI systems such as GitHub Actions, Jenkins, or GitLab CI.

 - Hands-on experience with sensors, motors, and data acquisition (DAQ), PLC, or microcontroller-based test systems; practical skills in mechanical assembly, wiring, and basic fabrication.

 - Understanding of hardware–firmware interactions, digital and analog I/O, and embedded interfaces such as CAN, Ethernet, UART, SPI, or I2C. Ability to read schematics and wiring diagrams and use lab instruments to bring up and troubleshoot hardware safely.

 - Strong troubleshooting skills across mechanical, electrical, firmware, and software systems, with a methodical approach to reproducing failures and identifying root causes.

 - Clear technical writing and the ability to work across engineering teams to translate requirements and failure reports into repeatable tests.


PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

 - Experience with EtherCAT, real-time control systems, motor controllers, or multi-actuator robots.

 - Familiarity with ROS/ROS 2, Zenoh, NVIDIA Jetson platforms, or other robotics middleware and embedded compute systems.

 - Experience with real-time simulation, plant models, sensor emulation, or software-in-the-loop testing using MATLAB/Simulink, NI, dSPACE, or custom platforms.

 - Ability to read and modify embedded C/C++ or Rust for test hooks, firmware diagnostics, or interface debugging.

 - Experience with release manifests, dependency validation, automated provisioning, OTA and rollback testing, or robot authentication and device pairing.

 - Experience building test dashboards and databases, scaling shared test labs, or reducing flaky tests.

 - Experience operating a hardware lab, including equipment calibration and safety programs, or building robots end to end through professional work, robotics competitions, or makerspaces.
